assertions.name: e_- is idempotent in H_2(q) (exact, generic q)
assertions.source: Bezout split of the Hecke quadratic (thm:em-spectral-completeness)

assertions.name: sigma e_- = -q^{-1} e_- — singlet channel carries the unique negative root
Skein sigma - sigma^{-1} = h (one h per vertex-pair; C2.1 bookkeeping)

description: RT 2-loop derivation plan (PR #1495) sub-claim C2.3: the minus sign of the Schwinger term -h^2 alpha is FORCED by the Hecke quadratic in the antisymmetric/singlet channel.  Exact identities in H_2(q) = R[sigma]/(sigma^2 - h sigma - 1) (section 7a convention, eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}): the Bezout singlet projector e_- = (q - sigma)/(q + q^{-1}) is idempotent with sigma e_- = -q^{-1} e_- (the unique NEGATIVE braiding root, thm:em-spectral-completeness); Skein sigma - sigma^{-1} = h gives one h per vertex-pair (C2.1 bookkeeping); the connected double-crossing insertion acts as (sigma^2 - 1) e_- = -(h/q) e_- (negative for real q > 1) vs +(h q) on e_+.  The sign asymmetry IS the e_+/e_- split; no choice is made.  The full -h^2 alpha [2]_q/(8 pi) normalisation (RT zero-mode measure C1.3 + two charge insertions) remains open on PR #1495's track.

data.finding: C2.3 closed at the channel-algebra level: the Schwinger minus sign is the singlet channel's negative braiding root -q^{-1}; the connected 2-vertex insertion is -(h/q) on e_- vs +(h q) on e_+, and Skein gives the h-per-vertex-pair bookkeeping of C2.1.  Remaining for Identity 2: the RT zero-mode measure (C1.3) and the two alpha charge insertions.
